# `Q-16-7` — Invalid project type contribution

> An extension resolved a custom `project.type`, but its
> `contributes.project` fragment is unusable.

## What this means

An extension can define a custom project type, so a project can set
`project.type: my-org/my-type` and inherit configuration the extension
supplies. The extension declares this under `contributes.project` in
its `_extension.yml`.

Quarto found the extension your `project.type` names, but could not use
what it declares. This stops the render — unlike most extension
problems, there is no sensible way to continue, because the project
type decides how every document in the project is processed.

Four things make the fragment unusable:

- `contributes.project` is not a mapping.
- Its `project.type` is not a string.
- It names a base type that is not built-in. Chaining custom types —
  one extension's type inheriting from another's — is not supported.
- It names `book` or `manuscript`, which Quarto 2 does not implement
  yet.

The message names the extension and the path to its `_extension.yml`.

## Why this happens

- **A hand-written extension manifest** with `contributes.project` as
  a list rather than a mapping.
- **An extension built against Quarto 1**, where the constraints
  differ.
- **A base type that is itself a custom type**, usually an attempt to
  build a family of related project types by layering them.
- **A `book`-based extension**, which cannot work until Quarto 2
  implements the book project type.

## How to fix

This is a defect in the extension, not in your project — the fix
belongs in the extension's `_extension.yml`. A usable contribution
looks like this:

```yaml
title: My Project Type
version: 1.0.0
contributes:
  project:
    project:
      type: website
    format:
      html:
        theme: cosmo
```

The nested `project.type` names the **built-in base type** the custom
type builds on: `default` or `website`. Everything else in the
fragment is configuration merged into projects that use the type.

If you do not maintain the extension, report the problem to its
author. In the meantime, set `project.type` to a built-in type and
copy the configuration you need directly into `_quarto.yml`.
